subject: Post-demo: end-to-end response-time acceptance checklist & runbook sync
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@inframed.com>, Priya Reddy <priya@veridian.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: end-to-end response-time acceptance checklist & runbook sync

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Below is a concise recap and the immediate asks we agreed on for validating end-to-end response-time (95th/99th percentile) for the hosted offering vs your current provider. I want to make sure engineering has a clear checklist so we can scope a short POC (2 weeks) and provide an apples-to-apples latency comparison.

Call recap / acceptance targets
- Goal: demonstrate hosted API can meet Veridian's e2e service-level targets for the inference path (app -> model -> response).
- Target thresholds: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 420ms (these are the targets you said are required for production readiness).
- Traffic shape: ~1200 QPS peak in the west region, 95% requests short (<= 64 tokens), 5% long (avg 512 tokens), occasional burst to 2.5k concurrent connections during batch window.
- Streaming: client-side streaming (partial responses) used for long-form generation; requires sustained concurrency of ~120 streaming connections producing partial frames every 150-300ms.

Immediate engineering asks (what we need from you)
1) Traffic profile CSV (per-endpoint QPS, distribution of sequence lengths, percent streaming requests) — you mentioned you could send this (attachment: veridian_traffic_profile.csv).
2) Representative request/response payloads and any SDK behavior that affects connections (keep-alive, max concurrent sockets).
3) Confirmation of whether KV-cache/prefix-caching can be safely exercised in POC (we need sample prompt prefixes).
4) Any internal SLAs or slow-path behavior (e.g., third-party enrichment that spikes response times).

What Redwood will deliver for POC
- A 72-hour controlled run comparing your current provider and Redwood hosted endpoints using identical traffic replay.
- Per-route p50/p95/p99, tail traces, token-level timing breakdown, and streaming frame latency distribution.
- A short runbook for failure modes (fallback to smaller model variants, regional failover) and suggested production routing policy.

Attachments: veridian_traffic_profile.csv (pending from you), draft SLO acceptance checklist (attached for our internal template).

Next steps
- Sam / Priya: send traffic profile and sample payloads by EOD Monday (2027-06-14).
- Redwood (Karthik / Marissa): propose dates for the 72-hour POC and share the test harness instructions.
- Schedule 30-min alignment on Wednesday to confirm the traffic shaping and streaming test fixtures.

Thanks — happy to jump on quick call if anything needs clarifying.

--
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Attachments referenced: veridian_traffic_profile.csv, slo_acceptance_checklist.xlsx

From: Sam Cho <sam.cho@inframed.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya@veridian.ai>
Date: 2027-06-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: end-to-end response-time acceptance checklist & runbook sync

Jasmine — thanks for the tidy recap. Confirming we'll send the traffic profile and a small sample set of payloads by end of day Monday. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) The 2.5k concurrent number I quoted is for open HTTP connections during batch ingestion windows; sustained user-facing qps is closer to 1.2k as you noted.
2) We do about ~8% streaming requests during heavy-load periods. Streaming behavior does include partial frames (we push partial tokens every ~200ms).
3) We have an enrichment pipeline that hits a third-party service for ~12% of requests — that occasionally creates 400-600ms downstream variability. We'll mark those in the sample CSV so you can filter them in the comparison.

I'll attach the CSV in a follow-up email (small file). Also: could you confirm whether Redwood's hosted endpoints support long-lived HTTP/2 streams or do you use HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming? That will impact our client-side harness.

Sam
Sam Cho
Head of Platform Engineering, Inframed
sam.cho@inframed.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Sam Cho <sam.cho@inframed.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: end-to-end response-time acceptance checklist & runbook sync

Looping in the engineering runbook and proposed test plan. Sam — thanks for the clarifications. Response to your question about streaming: Redwood hosted supports both HTTP/1.1 chunked responses and HTTP/2 server-sent frames for streaming. For the purposes of an apples-to-apples comparison we'll match the client-side pattern you use today.

Attached: test-harness-instructions.md (short), and our SLO acceptance checklist template (slo_acceptance_checklist.xlsx). Key points from our side: 
- We'll run a paired comparison: feed replayed traffic to your current provider and to Redwood endpoints back-to-back in the same region to minimize network variance.
- We will instrument token-level timers, model decode time, network RTTs, and our gateway overhead. The acceptance criteria will use the end-to-end timings (app->response) with and without enrichment calls.
- For streaming: we'll measure frame-to-frame latency percentiles and tail distribution (we typically look at 99.9th for streaming frame gaps).

Proposed schedule:
- Mon 2027-06-21: final alignment call, confirm CSV and payloads.
- Tue 2027-06-22 00:00 - Wed 2027-06-24 00:00: 72-hour POC run (paired).
- Thu 2027-06-24: results deliverable and 60-min walkthrough.

Action items (owners):
- Sam: send CSV + sample payloads (by EOD 2027-06-14) — note we can accept a sanitized export.
- Jasmine: share test harness instructions and a short checklist for network settings to ensure socket keep-alive matches. (attached)
- Marissa: prepare the results dashboard template and the p95/p99 comparison table.

If that schedule looks good we'll lock the POC window.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
